A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inappropriate use of antibiotics is still a major problem in the treatment of infections caused by bacteria that are resistant to multiple antibiotics.
antibiotic therapy for multidrug-resistant infections is often not appropriate, especially because of incorrect dosing, and this is associated with lower eradication rates.
the use of antibiotics in infections caused by MBR is still a challenge, even in tertiary hospitals, and it should be improved in order to reduce the impact on microbial resistance.

the antibiotic dosing regimen must be carefully assessed, especially in patients with renal impairment, to avoid inappropriate antibiotic prescription and, thus, to improve patient outcomes.
